registrar_rulings.reason: The mapper's alias condition fails on the evidence: pork-chops' live crown (Sam's Club $2.52/lb, url /ip/17799324269) is 'Member's Mark Bone-In Pork Chops', and product-urls.json shows 6 of its 7 store cells are explicitly bone-in (Aldi 'Premium Bone-In Assorted', Baker's 'Loin End Chop Bone In', Walmart 'Loin Chops, Bone-In', Family Fare 'Bone In', Sam's 'Bone-In') — so pork-chops IS the bone-in price class and boneless is the same food in a different purchase form at a materially different $/lb, the same ruling the estate made on the bone-in/boneless chicken-thigh pair (boneless-skinless-chicken-thigh exists beside chicken-thighs). No other namespace carries it: boneless-pork-chops is absent from all three id files and has no feed cell; pork-loin (recipe-board) and pork-tenderloin are whole-primal purchases, not chops; recipe-floor-id-map has no bridging pair. FOLLOW-UP EDITS REQUIRED WITH THE MINT: (1) recipe-only namespace — recipe-board-everyday baseline + recipe-commodities.json; (2) include must REQUIRE the form word, e.g. 'boneless.{0,25}pork.{0,30}chops?' / 'pork\s+(?:loin\s+)?(?:ribeye\s+)?chops?.{0,20}boneless', and clone pork-chops' full ~40-pattern exclude list plus 'bone[\s-]?in', breaded/stuffed/seasoned/marinated; (3) add the allowlist pair (boneless-pork-chops, pork-chops) to commodity-dupe-allowlist.json with reason 'bone-in vs boneless, 15-25% bone, different $/lb class' so the daily audit never re-flags it; (4) DEFECT FOUND IN PASSING: pork-chops' Fareway cell is 'Boneless Pork Ribeye Chops' at $1.25 — a boneless product already contaminating the bone-in id's cheapest-cell math; that capture belongs to the new id and pork-chops' Fareway cell needs re-capture as bone-in, and pork-chops' own include ('pork\b.{0,25}\bchops?\b') will keep claiming boneless products unless it gains a 'boneless' exclude once the new id exists.
